title: Basic Prompt Injection (HelperBot)
summary: As documented, the attacker replaces the agent's instructions and can direct it to do things it was not designed to do. As implemented, the effect is an acknowledgement string.

LC.rationale: The attacker's chat message reaches the HelperBot handler directly with no authentication and no mediation; the handler matches the instruction-override regex and returns the scripted acknowledgement (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:660-667, src/challenges/index.js:98-137).

CP.rationale: Each request is answered on its own; the lab profile states other chat agents answer only the latest user turn and cross-session persistence exists only in MemoryBot, not HelperBot (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1841-1848, src/index.js:500-502).

AP.rationale: The effect is confined to the single HelperBot reply; no handoff or cross-principal propagation occurs, and A2A handoffs are declared but not implemented (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1711-1770).

RH.rationale: The sink is a fixed acknowledgement string; no evaluator, verifier, or reward channel is on the path, and no reward-hacking episode is documented for this challenge (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:660-667, src/agent-success-paths.js:21-70).

ES.rationale: HelperBot declares read_file, write_file, and search_web, but in the default simulated mode no tool executes; only scripted paths run, so no dynamic extension is bound on this path (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/core/agents.js:44-79, src/core/agents.js:747-752).

agentic_applicability.rationale: scored as modeled; default config is scripted. The lab models HelperBot as an LLM chatbot that accepts new instructions, but even as modeled it only returns text and no tools are passed to the model.
